title: Luma Batch 3 — competitor coverage & evidence-integrity board (v4 — unit charts, nav rail, click-to-pin provenance panel, dataviz layer per ADR-021)

findings.method: checked = every WCAG contrast pair the payload's colour choices actually use (37 pairs, re-derived in verify-encoding.py beside this file, independent of the four component specs' own verify-contrast.py scripts rather than trusted from them), plus 4 structural/interaction properties confirmed by driving the rendered page with headless Chrome over the DevTools protocol (CDP) rather than asserted from the source: (1) click-to-pin opens the panel and populates it from the 155-entry data map with the grid still present in the DOM and operable; (2) Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the exact trigger that opened it, verified by dispatching the key on the focused panel element (dispatching on `document` itself throws inside the handler because Document has no `.closest()` — a real edge case, not a real user path, since a real keydown's target is always an Element; recorded as a limit of the test, not the code); (3) keyboard activation (Enter) on a non-<button> role=button trigger opens the panel identically to a click; (4) scrollspy sets aria-current on the rail after the page settles post-scroll (verified at 1200ms; a 500ms wait was insufficient in headless and produced a false negative on first attempt, corrected before relying on it). found = 4: (a) the isotype cluster arrays initially stretched to their full 1fr grid track regardless of unit count, making a 28-unit cluster (loyalty) render inside a box sized for the widest possible row — fixed with width:fit-content, justify-self:start on .ciso so the bounding box hugs exactly the drawn units, which is the property that makes the box itself legible as 'this cluster's total denominator'; (b) the empty/closed detail panel was a real grid row reserving a full 100vh-tall white block below the footer before first use, because .shellgrid's single-column default still placed the <aside> as an implicit second row — fixed with .shellgrid:not(.panel-open) .panel{display:none}; (c) two CSS comments referenced the unpromoted proposal names inside literal angle brackets (<CfNavRail>, <CfDetailPanel>) which, being inside a <style> block, are not HTML-escaped and would read as component-tag-shaped text to any regex-based scanner (including this repo's own Gate B, though it happened not to fire because gate-b.py's component check only runs on Write/Edit and this session used Bash) — reworded to avoid angle brackets entirely; (d) all 155 click-to-pin triggers had aria-haspopup and aria-controls but no default aria-expanded, so a screen reader encountering any of them before first interaction had no way to know they were togglable — fixed by adding aria-expanded="false" to every generated trigger at source (verified: 155 occurrences in the output, matching the trigger count exactly). (5) the print pathway: CSS alone (`details.meta > *:not(summary){display:block!important}`, the same technique v2/v3 both used) does NOT reliably force a closed <details> element open in print in this environment — a real --print-to-pdf render before the fix showed the Meta section, and everything in it, silently absent from the printed document (confirmed by text-extracting the PDF with PyMuPDF: 0 of 9 expected phrases from the Meta body were present, only the summary's own always-visible text survived). v3's own print verification never actually tested this — it checked that VISIBLE background colours survived print-color-adjust, not that HIDDEN content became visible, so this defect could have been present in v2/v3 too and gone uncaught. Fixed with the standards-based mechanism instead of a CSS override: `beforeprint`/`afterprint` listeners toggle the actual `open` HTML attribute on the Meta element and restore its prior state afterward. Re-verified: the same PDF render after the fix contains 'Changed from v3 to v4' and 'Claim format', going from 7 pages/1366 extracted words to 9 pages/2047 words with no other change to the page.

notes.why_a_new_id_and_not_ART-016_v4: Same convention every prior version bump in this repository has used (ART-001→002, ART-003→004, ART-008→009, ART-013→014, ART-013(v1)/ART-014(v2)→ART-016(v3)): a new sequential ART id per version, the immediately-prior version recorded in supersedes and named again in inputs.artifacts.
notes.directory_still_says_v4: ADR-003's directory contract versions by slug, independent of the registry id.
notes.what_changed_and_why: The owner's verdict on v3 was structural, not incremental: 'still UI bad — more data visualization graphics, design, navigation and progressive disclosure.' This is not a fix pass on v3 (that was v2→v3's job, against two attacking reports); it is a rebuild of the same evidence (ART-011/ART-012, unchanged) into a dashboard rather than an essay with tables. Five moves, each named in ADR-021 or the dispatch: (1) the 770-cell cluster view and the 112-cell journey view are now isotype/dot unit charts, not a percentage bar or a table of coloured cells — chart anatomy under ADR-021, not the component membrane; (2) every colour-key legend is removed (.legend14/.chartlegend/.legend from v3 do not exist in v4) — row/column headers plus per-cell mono labels carry the meaning directly; (3) a sticky nav rail with scrollspy and hash-addressable deep links replaces scroll-to-find, informed by ART-019's token math but instantiated as plain <nav>+<a>, never as <CfNavRail>, since that component remains unpromoted and the membrane is unchanged by ADR-021; (4) every row and every one of 155 marks (112 journey cells + 14 fourteen-rows + 10 cluster rows + 14 spotlight cells + 5 scoreboard rows) is a click-to-pin trigger opening a side panel with full provenance while the grid stays visible, informed by ART-020's focus-management contract but instantiated as a plain <aside>, never as <CfDetailPanel>, for the same membrane reason; (5) prose is cut hard — see validation.md for the measured before/after using the same reusable wordcount.py v3 shipped, run against both files.
notes.membrane_and_dataviz_boundary: ADR-021 was accepted at Gate A during this dispatch (status changed from PROPOSED to ACCEPTED on 2026-09-03 while this artifact was in progress — confirmed by re-reading the file, not assumed from the brief). Its consequence for cf-unit-cell (ART-017) is unconditional: chart anatomy, no promotion needed, no index entry. Its consequence for cf-chip/cf-nav-rail/cf-detail-panel (ART-018/019/020) is explicitly the opposite: 'remain components. The membrane applies to all three, unchanged.' None of the three has been promoted (checked directly: design-system/component-index.json has no cf-chip, cf-nav-rail or cf-detail-panel entry, and no ADR promotes any of them) so this payload does not instantiate them — no <CfChip>, <CfNavRail> or <CfDetailPanel> tag appears anywhere, including inside CSS comments (checked and one early draft slip corrected, see findings.method item c). The nav rail, the per-cell classification marks and the detail panel are built as page-local, on-token HTML/CSS/JS informed by the three specs' measured contrast tables and interaction contracts, which is the same category of artifact-local pattern v1–v3 already used for .kpi/.spot/.tierchip without a component-index entry, and it is verified against Gate B's actual mechanical check (gate-b.py's component regex only matches PascalCase JSX-shaped tags; it does not fire on lowercase HTML), not merely against a reading of the prose rule.
notes.correction_to_this_dispatch's_own_brief: The brief states ADR-021 is 'just accepted' as a fact to read before starting. At the moment this dispatch actually opened the file (before any writing began), its Status line read 'PROPOSED — Gate A, awaiting human decision', not accepted — the brief was accurate to a state that had not yet occurred in this session's own timeline, or was written anticipating an approval that had not yet landed. The file changed under this dispatch mid-session (a system reminder surfaced the diff) to 'ACCEPTED — Gate A, human decision recorded 2026-09-03' before any payload work depended on the distinction, so the brief's claim is true as of delivery — but it was not true at the instant this dispatch was told to treat it as settled, and a dispatch that had trusted the brief's tense without re-reading the file would have built on a decision that had not yet been made. Recorded per this repository's own standing instruction that a correction found in one's own brief should be stated, not silently absorbed.
